summary: RAF Fairford (IATA: FFD, ICAO: EGVA) is a Royal Air Force station in Gloucestershire, England, near the Cotswolds village of Fairford. Built during World War II, it is now a forward operating base used by the United States Air Force and NATO, with one of the UK's longest runways. It is best known to the public as the home of the Royal International Air Tattoo (RIAT), held most years in July.
faqs:
Q: Does RAF Fairford have commercial passenger flights?
A: No. RAF Fairford is a military airfield and does not handle scheduled commercial passenger services; public access is normally limited to special events such as RIAT.

Q: What is the Royal International Air Tattoo?
A: RIAT is one of the world's largest military airshows, usually held at RAF Fairford in July. It features flying displays, static aircraft, and international air forces.

Q: Can I visit RAF Fairford outside of RIAT?
A: Generally no. The station is active military property and is not open to the public except during organized events or official visits.

Q: How long is the runway at RAF Fairford?
A: Its main runway (09/27) is approximately 3,046 metres (9,993 ft), making it one of the longest in the UK and suitable for heavy bombers and large transport aircraft.
transport_tips: RAF Fairford has no railway station or regular public bus service to the base. Most visitors drive; during RIAT, use official park-and-ride sites and shuttle buses from Swindon and surrounding areas. The nearest main rail station is Swindon, about 15 miles away, with taxis or event buses available.
local_tip: For RIAT, the western end near the main gate often has the best static display access, but the eastern Kempsford side can offer good departure views if you arrive early and respect road closures and private land.
